description: The shared presets of yuanying/renovate-config hold the two-day wait, the ubuntu exception, the github-actions group, and the merge of patch, digest and pinning updates once the pull request's checks pass. A code owner's approval is also needed before anything reaches main (.github/CODEOWNERS), so such a pull request is merged once one of them approves it. CI runs on every pull request, with no paths filter, and builds every image, so every branch Renovate opens is tested before it is merged. What is merged this way reaches a release on its own through the weekly release

customManagers.description: The Node of the images is read as a Node release rather than as a Docker tag. A tag such as 24.22.2-trixie-slim is pushed again each time its Debian layer is rebuilt, so its time is not when that Node came out, and the two-day wait could hold the images back while setup-node moves on alone. Read from the Node releases, both carry the same time. The variant after the version is kept as written. The end-to-end test's images start from the same Node

The Go that builds the Sentinel's image is read as a Go release rather than as a Docker tag, for the same reason as the Node above, so that it moves on the same day as the go directive of go.mod that CI builds with
kubectl uses the Kubernetes release tag in dl.k8s.io URLs
Helm uses the release tag in get.helm.sh archive and checksum names
Only kustomize/v tags are CLI releases; kyaml and other module releases are not. The fetch script adds kustomize/ to the version
sops uses the release tag in both download URLs and asset names
gh asset names omit the v; the fetch script adds it to the release URL
vmctl is released by vmapi, with the v in both the release tag and archive name
a2a asset names omit the v; the fetch script adds it to the release URL
sdctl's releases carry no binary; the sandbox's image builds it with go install at the release's tag, which keeps the v
porkadot is not on RubyGems; the sandbox's image builds its gem from a tag of its repository, so its version is read from the repository's tags

packageRules.description: The runner uses pi-ai types with pi-coding-agent, which depends on the exact same pi-ai release. Updating only one installs two pi-ai versions whose private event-stream types are incompatible. Keep these two direct dependencies on one branch

The Node the images run (the Dockerfile's) and the Node the tests run (setup-node in ci.yml and release.yml) are the same version on purpose: a test passing on one Node says little about another. Grouping them puts them on one branch, so they cannot drift apart one pull request at a time. This takes setup-node's Node out of the shared github-actions group
The Go that builds the image (the Dockerfile's) and the Go that CI builds and tests with (go.mod's go directive, which setup-go reads) are kept the same in one branch, as the Node is
The same Node and Go are read by the custom managers above, from their releases. Left on, the dockerfile manager would propose them a second time under the Docker tags' times

The kustomize examples (deploy/kubernetes/example/ and migrate/) name the images of one release, always the same version. Grouping them moves the four on one branch, so the example is never left with two versions

@types/node describes the Node the code runs on, and its major follows Node's. A new major of it arrives before that Node is an LTS release the images can take, and type-checking against it would accept APIs the runtime lacks. Its major is raised by hand together with the node group

Astryx is in beta: a 0.x release can change components and how they look even in a patch, which CI does not see. Its packages are pinned and move together on one branch, merged by hand after the screens are looked at
